Feast of Firstfruits
FEEST of FURST-froots
n. phrase
Firstfruits: the first-ripe portion of any harvest, offered to the LORD; Hebrew rē’shīth (first, beginning) or bikkūrīm (firstfruits). The OT feast prescribed in Leviticus 23:9-14, observed the day after the Passover Sabbath as the wave-offering of the first-ripe barley sheaf.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Feast of Firstfruits was the second of the three great pilgrimage feasts of Israel (following Passover/Unleavened Bread) and the inaugurating event of the fifty-day count to Pentecost. Leviticus 23:9-14 prescribes the observance. On the day after the Sabbath of Passover week, the priest waved before the LORD a sheaf of the first-ripe barley harvest, accompanied by a lamb of the first year for a burnt offering, a meal offering of flour and oil, and a drink offering of wine. Until this wave-offering was made, no Israelite was to eat any of the new harvest’s bread, parched grain, or green ears—the firstfruits had to be presented to the LORD first, in acknowledgment that the whole harvest belonged to Him and was received as His gift. The structural significance of firstfruits in biblical theology is deep. First, the principle: the firstfruits represent the whole harvest. By presenting the first-ripe portion to the LORD, the offerer acknowledges that the whole crop is the LORD’s gift; what is given is the consecrating-portion that sanctifies the rest. Romans 11:16: for if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. Second, the typological fulfillment in Christ. 1 Corinthians 15:20-23 makes the doctrine explicit: but now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming. The risen Christ is the Firstfruits of the resurrection-harvest. He rose on the day after the Passover Sabbath—the exact day of the OT wave-offering of firstfruits—and His resurrection is the consecrating earnest of the great resurrection-harvest of His people at His return. Third, the ecclesial application: the church and believers are themselves named firstfruits. James 1:18: of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. Rom 16:5: Epaenetus is named the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ. 1 Cor 16:15: the household of Stephanas is the firstfruits of Achaia. Rev 14:4: the 144,000 are firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb. The firstfruits-category therefore extends across the canon: Israel as firstfruits to the LORD; Christ as Firstfruits of the resurrection; the church as firstfruits of God’s creatures; particular saints as firstfruits of their regions. Each instance preserves the principle: the firstfruits is the consecrating earnest, anticipating and guaranteeing the full harvest that follows.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines FIRSTFRUITS as the first or earliest produce; the fruit gathered first in the season; in scripture, the OT Feast of Firstfruits (Lev 23:9-14) prescribed the wave-offering of the first-ripe barley; typologically fulfilled in Christ the Firstfruits of the resurrection (1 Cor 15:20) and applied to the church and believers as firstfruits of God’s creatures.

FIRSTFRUITS, n. — 1. The first or earliest produce of any thing, as the fruit which first ripens. 2. In scripture, the offerings made to the LORD of the first portion of any harvest, which sanctified the whole; the OT Feast of Firstfruits (Lev 23:9-14). 3. Figuratively, Christ as the Firstfruits of the resurrection (1 Cor 15:20), the church as firstfruits of God’s creatures (Jas 1:18).

📖 Key Scripture

Leviticus 23:10-11 — "Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest: And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it."

1 Corinthians 15:20 — "But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept."

Romans 11:16 — "For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches."

James 1:18 — "Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The firstfruits-doctrine is corrupted, on one side, by the prosperity-and-tithing-emphasis traditions that have reduced firstfruits to a fundraising principle (give the first-ripe of your income, and the LORD will bless the rest) without the deeper Christological and ecclesial substance the OT feast anticipates—and on the other by the general loss of typological reading that has dropped Christ-as-Firstfruits-of-the-resurrection from active preaching.

expand to see more

The prosperity-and-tithing-emphasis traditions have, in various forms, reduced firstfruits to a fundraising principle: give the first and best of your income to the LORD (or to His ministry, conveniently identified with the soliciting institution), and the LORD will bless what remains. There is a biblical pattern of firstfruits-giving from which this draws (Prov 3:9-10: honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine), but the principle is broader than fundraising and the substance is deeper than transactional return. The biblical firstfruits is the consecrating earnest that sanctifies the whole—and the supreme firstfruits is not the believer’s tithe but Christ’s resurrection, by which the whole resurrection-harvest of His people is sanctified and guaranteed. The recovery is the recovery of the doctrinal depth, with the practical principle of firstfruits-giving as one application of the broader theological substance, not the substance itself.

The general loss of typological reading has dropped Christ-as-Firstfruits-of-the-resurrection from active preaching in many traditions. Yet 1 Corinthians 15:20-23 makes the typology structural to the doctrine of the resurrection: Christ rose on the morrow after the sabbath (the exact day of the OT firstfruits wave-offering), and His resurrection is named the firstfruits of them that slept. The argument has enormous pastoral weight. The same Christ who rose is the Firstfruits whose resurrection consecrates and guarantees the resurrection of His people. The believer’s resurrection is not a vague hope but a covenantally-secured certainty, with Christ’s resurrection-firstfruits as its earnest. Where the typology is lost, the doctrine of bodily resurrection becomes a peripheral or even doubted teaching; where the typology is restored, the resurrection of the saints stands as firmly as the resurrection of Christ Himself, of which it is the harvest-conclusion. Recover both ends. Refuse the prosperity-reduction that flattens firstfruits to fundraising principle, and refuse the loss of typology that drops Christ-as-Firstfruits from the resurrection-doctrine. The biblical Feast of Firstfruits stands at the heart of the gospel’s resurrection-substance, with Christ’s rising on the day of the wave-offering of firstfruits as the consecrating earnest of every saint’s bodily resurrection at His return.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rē’shīth (first, beginning) and bikkūrīm (firstfruits); Greek aparchē (firstfruits); the OT Feast of Firstfruits (Lev 23:9-14) and its typological fulfillment in Christ the Firstfruits of the resurrection (1 Cor 15:20) and the church as firstfruits of God’s creatures (Jas 1:18).

expand to see more

Hebrew rē’shīth (H7225) — first, beginning, firstfruits (Gen 1:1, “in the beginning”; Prov 3:9, the firstfruits of all thine increase).

Hebrew bikkūrīm (H1061) — firstfruits (the plural specific to the harvest-firstfruits).

Greek aparchē (G536) — firstfruits (9 NT uses; Rom 8:23; 11:16; 16:5; 1 Cor 15:20, 23; 16:15; 2 Thess 2:13; Jas 1:18; Rev 14:4).

Hebrew chag ha-bikkūrīm — Feast of Firstfruits (the OT festival name).
